answer: Scarce-contest scheduling. Each identity must win a recurring compute slot by submitting work that survives a ferrous-content assay of its claimed sensor provenance; the assay is cheap to verify but requires unique physical material, so duplicates collapse. A comet's trajectory model supplies the rotating challenge set, letting verifiers rerun the assay without storing state. Because a gale of forged submissions still needs one assay per identity per epoch, an attacker's marginal cost scales with distinct credentialed hardware, not wallet count.
